text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Truong My Hoa was reelected as President of the Vietnam Women's Union at the Eighth Women's Congress, which ended on Tuesday in Hanoi.
-- The Vietnam National Committee of AIDS Prevention had recorded a total of 5,717 HIV/AIDS cases nationwide by the end of last week.

-- A proposal to stop selling foreign currency to companies with foreign investment, which is aimed at boosting the country's foreign currency reserves and tackling its growing trade deficit, has been submitted to Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet by the State Bank.
-- Two Royal Thai Navy ships will arrive in Ho Chi Minh City's port on Wednesday for a three-day friendship visit aimed at strengthening cooperation between the Thai and Vietnamese navies.

-- The first Vietnamese ambassador to the United States, Le Van Bang, said his prority for the immediate future is to step up cultural, technological, economic and trade relations between the two countries.

-- President Le Duc Anh had sent a letter inviting Russian President Boris Yeltsin to visit Vietnam to strengthen the traditional relations and cooperation between the two countries. In response, Boris Yeltsin sent his thanks for the invitation and said he would be pleased to see Le Duc Anh in Moscow.
-- President Le Duc Anh has called for more efforts to reduce damage caused by natural disasters.

-- Politburo member Le Kha Phieu, speaking at a training course for high-ranking members of the Communist Party, has called for further expansion of the socialist democracy and more efficient state organs.
-- The Southern Steel company has produced 76,867 tonnes of steel so far this year, equivalent to 30 percent of its target for the whole year.
